questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Points of Intersection of a Hyperbola and a Horizontal or Vertical Line
questions.problem: Calculate the points where the hyperbola ${x}^{2}-{y}^{2}=12$ intersects the line $x=-4.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $x=-4,$ we substitute $x=-4$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-{y}^{2} & =12 \\ (-4)^{2}-{y}^{2} & =12 \\ 16-{y}^{2} & =12 \\ -{y}^{2} & =12-16 \\ -{y}^{2} & =-4 \\ {y}^{2} & =4 \\ y & =\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the hyperbola intersects the vertical line $x=-4$  at the points $(-4,\pm 2).$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Points of Intersection of a Hyperbola and a Line
questions.problem: Calculate the $x$-coordinates of the points where the hyperbola $14{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}=50$ intersects the line $y=2x.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $y=2x,$ we first replace $y$ with $2x$ in the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}14{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2} & =50 \\ 14{x}^{2}-3(2x)^{2} & =50 \\ 14{x}^{2}-12{x}^{2} & =50 \\ 2{x}^{2} & =50 \\ {x}^{2} & =25 \\ x & =\pm 5\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Calculate the $x$-coordinates of the points where the hyperbola $5{y}^{2}-16{x}^{2}=36$ intersects the line $y=-2x.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $y=-2x,$ we first replace $y$ with $-2x$ in the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{y}^{2}-16{x}^{2} & =36 \\ 5(-2x)^{2}-16{x}^{2} & =36 \\ 5(4{x}^{2})-16{x}^{2} & =36 \\ 20{x}^{2}-16{x}^{2} & =36 \\ 4{x}^{2} & =36 \\ {x}^{2} & =9 \\ x & =\pm 3\end{aligned}
$$

choices.value: There are no points of intersection

questions.problem:
From **top to bottom,** the $y$-intercepts of the hyperbola $6{y}^{2}-5{x}^{2}=30$ are

questions.worked_solution:
To find the $y$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{y}^{2}-5{x}^{2} & =30 \\ 6{y}^{2}-5(0)^{2} & =30 \\ 6{y}^{2} & =30 \\ {y}^{2} & =5 \\ y & =\pm \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

So, from top to bottom, the $y$-intercepts are $(0,\sqrt{5})$ and $(0,-\sqrt{5}).$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Y-Intercepts of a Hyperbola
questions.problem:
From **top to bottom,** the $y$-intercepts of the hyperbola $\frac{(y-5)^{2}}{9}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}=1$ are

$($
{{field-1}}, 
{{field-2}} $)\,$
and
$\,($
{{field-3}}, 
{{field-4}} $).$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the $y$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(y-5)^{2}}{9}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{8} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-5)^{2}}{9}-\frac{(0)^{2}}{8} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-5)^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ (y-5)^{2} & =9 \\ y-5 & =\pm 3 \\ y & =5\pm 3\end{aligned}
$$

So, from top to bottom, the $y$-intercepts are $(0,8)$ and $(0,2).$
